gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of full-rated sun each feeder's own solar panel needs to refill its battery from empty. Birdfy's spec sheets give about 16.7 h for the 4K Feeder Metal 2 (9,000 mAh on a 2 W roof), 11.1 h for the Feeder 2 Pro (3 W) and 9.6 h for the Feeder Wood (5,200 mAh, 2 W). Notebookcheck's spec table for the Kiwibit Bird Feeder 2 gives about 4.4 h (5,200 mAh, 4.4 W). So at the 4–6 h of daily direct sun that makers ask for, the Birdfy 4K needs about 3–4 sunny days to refill, while the Kiwibit needs about one.
standout_why: BirdFeederLab (#3, solar-specific, opened 2026-11-09) gives no battery mAh or panel wattage for any pick. It only offers the general 'makers recommend 4–6 hours of direct sun' line. I could not open the two cited pages: WIRED (#2) and Good Housekeeping (#11) blocked the fetcher, and a curl attempt needed approval. So I can't rule out that they give a mAh or wattage figure. Neither is known to divide one by the other into refill hours. ChatGPT's answer itself only says '5W solar panel' for Soliom and 'solar roof' for Bird Buddy, with no battery-to-panel ratio.
decides: This changes the 'best for solar' pick but not the 'best camera' pick. The higher-end Birdfy 4K and metal models pair big 9,000 mAh batteries with 2 W roofs, so in short winter days their solar roof only slows the drain and you may have to take the camera in to charge it. The Kiwibit Bird Feeder 2 (4.4 W on 5,200 mAh) and the Birdfy Feeder 2 Pro or Duo (3 W or 5 W external panels) come closest to running on solar alone. Notebookcheck (Stephen Pereyra) still calls even the Kiwibit's 4.4 W roof 'more of a charge maintainer.' A shopper who mostly wants never to unplug the camera should weight panel-to-battery ratio above video resolution.
